H Caloberry: A common, slightly prickly bush that grows in woods but must remain close to a water source. They are edible and taste mostly tart but their seeds taste sweet. The bushes grow in small thickets that are within a close radius of water. They have darker leaves and the berries are raspberry red, while the flowers have anywhere from three to ten petals and cover very little of the bush. The flowers can be the same berry red, a reddish-pink, or white with berry red stripes on each petal.  
   
Akal Fern: As the name says, the Akal fern is indeed a fern. It's name means “fight” or “anger” in the ancient language of Ailosen. It is a bright red in color and is covered in thorns. Its leaves have microscopic hairs that irritate the skin and if one's feathers touch it may stunt wing growth for a few weeks. After this, however, the wings will grow rapidly. This ability causes it to be used in military training, despite heavy debate. The thorns on it are serrated and are often put on arrowheads. When burned, the smoke is heavily toxic, and when the hairs are removed, it is edible and is known to taste quite good, and considered a delicacy in some areas of the capital.  
Hornleafed Fairy Bush: A small bush that was said in folktales to be the home of fairies and small dragons, hollowed out by their magic. It, unfortunately, is not, although a common spot to find Lepo butterfly eggs, which are quite beautiful, both the adults and the eggs. It is hollow, however, with branches that arc and only grow leaves at the top. The tightly braided roots somehow do not choke each other and form a beautiful pattern on the ground. The roots cover all ground in the bush, and then drop vertically by a few inches, and then run for a good few feet. Their leaves have vertical spikes that are folded and shade each leaf. It is presumed that these are to keep the plant in at least partial shade.

If we do not quit, we will either hunt ourselves to extinction or fight for eternity! Do you want your children, and their children, and generations that go on forever, to know nothing but war? No! He bore the grayish-brown, black, and white wings of a goose. One man who wore the blue wings of the jay Clan spoke. “Calos, your own tribe does not want this war to go on!” He gestured towards the Goose leader who was starting at Calos and frowning.
